newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire House votes to hike tobacco tax.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire House votes to hike tobacco tax.

text.p: The New Hampshire House of Representatives on Thursday passed legislation raising the state tobacco tax 20 cents a pack to help erase a deficit and fund kindergartens and a biennial budget.
The tax is currently 25 cents on cigarettes, cigars and snuff and smokeless tobacco and generates $45 million annually. Lawmakers passed the increase recommended by the House Finance Committee.

Gov. Jeanne Shaheen had proposed a 25 cent increase to erase a $37 million budget deficit inherited from GOP former Gov. Stephen Merrill, fund a $20 million state workers' contract and pay for a statewide kindergarten plan.
House Finance Committee Chairman Neal Kurk said the 20 cent rise will address all of Shaheen's programs.
Shaheen said she can live with the 20 cent increase.
"It allows us to get the revenues we need to go forward with the budget," she said.
Without debate, the House passed a $5.6 billion biennial budget recommended by House budget writers that is only a few million dollars less than one crafted by Shaheen.
The cigarette tax increase and the biennial budget will go before the Senate Finance Committee next week.
